mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth is below -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month periods of sustained INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust demand across consumption and investment channels, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both show YoY growth > 2% in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and HOUST show YoY growth > 2% in the same quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during five-month stretches where PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months, irrespective of GDP growth, signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month MA for three consecutive months, regardless of GDP growth.
